summary_paragraph: An elderly female with a history of chronic diastolic heart failure, hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, and recurrent DVT/PE presented with acute mid-epigastric abdominal pain, vomiting, and obstipation. Imaging revealed a partial small bowel obstruction with a 4.7 cm linear foreign body at the transition point in the distal ileum, likely the cause. She was managed conservatively with bowel rest, IV fluids, and monitoring. Her symptoms resolved, and a follow-up CT showed resolution of the obstruction. She also had a urinary tract infection, treated with antibiotics. Her INR was elevated at 3.6, so Coumadin was held and she was referred to the anticoagulation clinic. She remained hemodynamically stable, advanced to a regular diet, and was discharged home with instructions to continue antibiotics, hold anticoagulation, and follow up with her primary and specialty providers.
